learnings.insight: navbarResponsive.test.tsx asserts a Tailwind display CONTRACT (has `hidden`, has `sm:inline-flex`, and NOT a bare inline-flex via /(?<![-\w:])inline-flex(?![-\w])/) rather than a computed style, because happy-dom/renderToStaticMarkup does not run the CSS engine. This is a legitimate unit-level proxy AS LONG AS the negative guard (no bare inline-flex) is present — that guard is what makes the failure mode behavioral (the exact same-specificity leak) instead of a rename. A class-presence-only assertion without the negative guard WOULD be rename-only and rejectable. Both fail-first proofs pass this bar.
learnings.action: reviewer: when a test asserts responsive CSS via class strings, confirm it also asserts the ABSENCE of the conflicting utility, not just presence of the intended one — presence alone survives the very bug it should catch.
